What We Do

Full-Service Bariatric Surgery Revenue Cycle Management

Bariatric surgery billing is among the most prior-authorization-intensive specialties in medicine. Commercial payers require BMI documentation, comorbidity evidence, documented failed conservative treatment, and psychological clearance before authorizing procedures. PMEX manages the full authorization process and all surgical coding.

Bariatric Procedure Coding

Sleeve gastrectomy (43775), gastric bypass (43644), and band procedures coded from the operative report.

Prior Authorization Management

Full auth package compiled: BMI, comorbidities, diet failure, psych clearance, sleep study.

Laparoscopic vs. Open Coding

Laparoscopic and open bariatric CPT codes confirmed from the operative report approach.

Revisional Bariatric Surgery

Revision and conversion procedure codes billed with prior failed procedure documentation.

Post-Op Global Period Management

90-day global period tracked with correct post-op visit billing and modifier management.

Metabolic Surgery Billing

Metabolic surgery for Type 2 diabetes coded and authorized under metabolic vs. bariatric criteria.

Sound Familiar?

Common Bariatric Surgery Billing Problems

Each problem below is one PMEX resolves before it costs you revenue.

Prior authorization submitted without the required 6-month supervised diet documentation.

PMEX compiles the full auth package including supervised diet records before submitting any bariatric authorization.

Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy coded as open procedure, or vice versa.

PMEX reads the operative report to confirm approach and codes laparoscopic vs. open per the documented technique.

Psychological clearance not included in the authorization package, auth denied.

PMEX tracks all required clearance documents and confirms psych clearance is on file before submitting auth.

Revisional bariatric surgery denied because prior failed procedure documentation is incomplete.

PMEX compiles documentation of the prior bariatric procedure before submitting the revision authorization.

Post-op visits billed during the 90-day global period without modifier 24 for new conditions.

PMEX tracks the global period per procedure and routes post-op visits to the correct billing path.

Sleep apnea comorbidity not included in the auth, reducing the medical necessity score.

PMEX includes all documented comorbidities including sleep apnea, diabetes, and hypertension in every auth submission.

Denial Management

Top Denial Patterns in Bariatric Surgery Billing

Bariatric practices lose 20 to 35 percent of revenue to prior authorization failures, documentation gaps, and global period violations.

PATTERN 01

Authorization Denied, Supervised Diet Not Documented

Gastric sleeve authorization submitted. Commercial payer requires 6 months of physician-supervised dietary counseling documented in the chart. Records submitted covered only 4 months. Auth denied. Surgery delayed. Patient and practice both impacted.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX tracks the supervised diet period from the first documented visit and confirms 6 full months of physician-supervised dietary counseling are documented in the records before submitting the bariatric prior authorization.

PATTERN 02

Laparoscopic Bariatric Coded as Open

Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy performed (43775). Billing team submits open sleeve gastrectomy. On payer audit, the operative report confirms laparoscopic approach. Recoupment issued. Compliance exposure created from one approach coding error.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX reads the operative report before selecting any bariatric CPT code. Laparoscopic and open approaches have distinct codes. Approach is confirmed from the operative report on every bariatric case.

PATTERN 03

Revisional Surgery Denied, Failed Procedure Not Documented

Revision from gastric band to sleeve gastrectomy submitted. Payer requires documentation that the prior bariatric procedure failed, including weight regain records, nutritional counseling records, and physician documentation of band failure. Incomplete documentation submitted.

PMEX SOLUTION

PMEX compiles the full documentation package for revisional bariatric surgery before submitting the authorization, including operative record of the prior procedure, weight trend data, nutritional counseling records, and the treating surgeon documentation of failure criteria.

Questions

Bariatric Surgery Billing Questions Answered

Most commercial payers require: BMI of 40 or higher (or 35 with comorbidities), 6 months of physician-supervised dietary counseling, psychological clearance, sleep study, and documentation of comorbidities. Requirements vary by payer. We manage the full package.

Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy uses CPT 43775. Open sleeve gastrectomy uses a different code. Gastric bypass has distinct laparoscopic (43644) and open (43846) codes. We confirm the approach from the operative report before coding.

Major bariatric procedures have a 90-day global period. Routine post-op care is included in the surgical fee. New conditions arising during the global period are billed with modifier 24. We track global period end dates per patient.

Yes. Some commercial payers authorize metabolic surgery for Type 2 diabetes control with a lower BMI threshold than traditional bariatric surgery. We identify and pursue metabolic surgery authorization where applicable.

Revisional procedures require documentation of the prior bariatric surgery and the clinical rationale for revision. We compile the full documentation package before submitting the revision authorization.

Within 30 days, with prior authorization tracking and global period management active from day one.
